chapter_theme: The three states of the soul: kevala, alone with anava and knowing nothing; sakala, joined to body, maya and karma; and suddha, purified by grace. The chapter sorts beings by their impurities, subdivides each state into three and maps them onto waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond, and holds that bondage and release alike are Hara's grace, by which the soul, with maya as nurse and Siva as father, comes to purity.
structure_note: 2227 to 2236 introduce the three states and the beings in them; 2237 to 2239 the suddha state as the tattvas subside; 2240 to 2248 the classes of soul by their impurities; 2249 to 2254 the ninefold division and the waking states; 2255 to 2257 bondage and release as grace; 2258 to 2261 the states in the body and birth; 2262 to 2265 the way to purity; 2266 to 2268 a riddle, the tattva count and the closing family image.

2227.reading: The pure soul that knows itself, the kevala soul that is alone in itself, and the sakala soul that stands in division and difference are each joined to the real, the unreal and the real-unreal, according to their own work.
2227.nuance: The chapter's three names arrive at once: கேவலன் (alone, with anava only), சகலன் (joined to body and world) and சுத்தன் (pure). சத்து, அசத்து and சதசத்து are traditionally the Lord, the bonds and the soul between them, but line 3 is compressed and I can't fix how each soul is paired with each.

2228.reading: A person is his own enemy and his own friend, his own next world and this one, the one who eats the fruit of the deeds he did, and his own master.
2228.nuance: The fourfold தானே makes the soul answerable for its own state. Placed in a chapter that later says bondage and release both come by Hara's grace (2256), the last line (தனக்குத் தலைவனும்) reads as the soul's responsibility within its bound state, not as a denial of the Lord; that is my reading.

2229.reading: The soul in kevala moves into mahamaya; as maya lights it, it comes to knowledge, and as karma-born and maya-born impurity mingle with it, the bonds it takes on make the sakala state.
2229.nuance: காமியம் and மாமேயம் are taken as காமிய மலம் (the impurity of deeds) and மாயேய மலம் (the impurity of maya's products), which with anava make the three malas. எறிப்ப (strikes, or shines on) leaves open whether maya wakes the soul or wounds it; tradition takes maya as a lamp that gives the soul limited knowledge.

2230.reading: Those who enter the sakala state are the sakalas, joined to all three named impurities: the matchless lotus-born Brahma, Vishnu, the many long-lived gods, humans and everything down to the worm.
2230.nuance: The verse puts the high gods among bound souls with men and insects; status in the cosmos does not lift the three impurities. சீடம் is read as கீடம் (worm, insect), as in 2244.

2231.reading: Those who stay in all-spreading maya are the pralayakalas; of those in the other condition, with bodies, the ones of unfailing marks are Srikantha and, with him, the hundred and eight Rudras.
2231.nuance: பிரளயம் is taken as பிரளயாகலர், souls with two impurities. Srikantha and the 108 Rudras as a class of such beings is a Siddhanta teaching; line 2 (மேவிய மற்றது உடம்பாய்மிக் குள்ளன) is obscure.

2232.reading: Those in kevala who have anava alone are the vidyesvaras, Ananta and the others, the eight, the seventy million mantra beings and the many lords.
2232.nuance: These are the விஞ்ஞானகலர், souls with only anava left. எழுகோடி மந்திரர் are mantras as beings, not formulas. The repeated ஆகின்ற (that become) keeps the list a list of states, not of persons.

2233.reading: Among them, those who have received Siva's grace leave behind the praised bindu and nada as their impurity departs, become one with Om and are absorbed; being stainless, that is the work of the flawless suddha state.
2233.nuance: Bindu and nada, elsewhere the source of manifestation, are here something to be left behind. ஒம்மயம் is read as ஓம்மயம் (made of Om); ஒடுங்கல் is absorption or subsidence.

2234.reading: On inquiry there are three kinds and four kinds; these are kevala, maya and joined desire, which by their nature depart, and the Lord, gathering them up and setting them aside, cut away the impurity.
2234.nuance: மூவகை நால்வகை and சேர்இச்சை are obscure: perhaps three classes of souls and four impurities, with இச்சை standing for karma. The last line is clear: the Lord removes the impurity.

2235.reading: Leaving the false end of knowing and the thirty-six behind, so that ignorance departs, becoming the one he reached, entering the space that is the real moving and unmoving world, reaching without reaching: that is called the suddha state.
2235.nuance: ஆறாறு is the thirty-six tattvas. பொய்யான போதாந்தம் (the false end of knowing) may be knowledge that ends in the instruments, as against Siva-knowledge. எய்தாமல் எய்தும் is a deliberate paradox: union without arriving anywhere.

2236.reading: This soul, beginningless and bound, is driven by the five impurities that came without beginning; from beginningless kevala it is placed in sakala, and through beginningless births it comes into the suddha state.
2236.nuance: அனாதி begins every line: soul, impurities, kevala and births are all without beginning, yet the movement ends in purity. The five impurities are counted again in 2253 and 2257; tradition adds மாயேயம் and திரோதாயி to the three. பசுவியாத்தி is unclear.

2237.reading: Within the suddha state, beyond the kevala, as knowledge arises in the midst of turiya toward the supreme, one knows oneself by oneself, and that is the reality.
2237.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 (அந்தரம் ... தற்பரத்தின்பால்) are obscure and I have kept only their drift. தத்துவம் here seems to mean the truth itself, not a tattva in the list.

2238.reading: The twenty-five subside in the soul, and the soul too, seeing the truth, finds release in the suddha state; the three pure tattvas beginning with vidya, the ancient Shakti and the lord Siva appear in that order.
2238.nuance: ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as twenty-five lower tattvas. The pure tattvas are traditionally suddha vidya, isvara, sadakhya, shakti and siva, which fits வித்தை முதன்மூன்றும் with Shakti and Siva.

2239.reading: The twenty-five and the six subside into the soul, the three above are reached in true yoga, and seeing the Shakti held in Siva's portion, one subsides as one reaches the four-sevens.
2239.nuance: 25 + 6 + 3 approaches the thirty-six with Shakti and Siva, but நாலேழ் (four sevens, twenty-eight, or four and seven) does not fit any count I can fix. சிவபாகம் may be Siva's half, the Shakti who is his left side.

2240.reading: Those with anava alone, who know nothing, are the kevalas; those who hold maya are the pralayakalas; and those who take on all three bonds are the sakalas, who have visible form and see without seeing.
2240.nuance: காணும் உருவினர் காணாமை காண்பவே may mean the sakalas see only with bodily eyes and so do not truly see. The verse is a key to the chapter's classes.

2241.reading: For the vijnanakalas the impurity is anava; for the pralayakalas, maya; for the sakalas, anava, maya and karma, all three, are the impurities shown.
2241.nuance: Later Siddhanta texts give the pralayakalas anava and karma, without maya, since maya is dissolved at pralaya. This verse, with 2240 and 2243, ties them to maya instead. Whether that is an older scheme or a looser use of மாயை I can't say.

2242.reading: The vijnanakalas rise within kevala by the power of bindu that rises there, and the mantra beings who pass from kevala into sakala in the world have mahamaya as their truth.
2242.nuance: பூவயின் (in the world, or in the flower) and the syntax of lines 3 and 4 are unclear. The tradition makes mahamaya (pure maya, bindu) the field of the higher beings, as impure maya is of the sakalas.

2243.reading: The pralayakalas who dwell in maya come so that maya does not appear, and those in the maya-sakala of anava, karma and mahamaya are called the hundred and eight Rudras.
2243.nuance: ஏயமன் is obscure, and the relation of the 108 Rudras to 2231 is not settled by the verse.

2244.reading: Those whom the three impurities join, embrace and bewilder are the sakalas of that body: gods, devas and men, and truly, from Brahma down to the many insects, sakalas enter wombs in due order and are bound.
2244.nuance: யோனிபுக்கு (entering the womb) makes sakala the state of birth itself. The list from வேதா to கீடம் matches 2230.

2245.reading: Those steeped in the suddha state become pure when the three impurities, real and unreal, run off, and each bond in turn, the maddening darkness, is let go entirely by the ray that is Siva.
2245.nuance: மத்த இருள் (intoxicating darkness) is traditionally anava, and சிவனான கதிர் the light of grace. சத்துஅசத்து may name the impurities as both real and unreal, or the soul's two sides.

2246.reading: Tat-kevala is release, solitude itself; afterward sakala is separation from kala and the rest; the suddha-kevala named in words is waking, and what one does within oneself is one's own purity.
2246.nuance: Each line pairs a technical name with a gloss I can't fix. The verse seems to begin the subdivision of each state that 2249 to 2252 set out.

2247.reading: Kevala is the soul without knowledge, not joined to raga and the other tattvas, without any mark, eternal, unjoined to kala, without action, and pervaded by impurity.
2247.nuance: முத்தன் (freed) at the start seems ironic: the kevala soul is 'free' of the tattvas only because it has nothing. தினங்கற்ற வல்லோன் கிறியன் is obscure.

2248.reading: Bindu and maya, the kriya that comes with them, the ever-present supreme power of knowledge and the purifying of the body; the pralayakalas who gain the true knowledge of bindu; and the sakala and suddha souls who come into the world.
2248.nuance: The verse is a list without a main verb, and I can't tell how its items relate. It may be naming what belongs to each class of soul.

2249.reading: If the divisions of kevala and the others are told, the three kevalas rise within sakala, and there the three of suddha too, so that the unceasing nine are known to those who perceive them.
2249.nuance: The next three verses set out the nine: kevala, sakala and suddha, each within each. Line 3 (மதிசுத்த மூடவே) is obscure.

2250.reading: Kevala within kevala is the beyond-beyond; sakala within kevala is the bindu-born state; suddha within kevala belongs to the faultless vijnanakalas, and there the Lord is the form of grace.
2250.nuance: அதீதாதீதம் and வயிந்தவம் are technical. Line 3 reads கேவத் திறசுத்தம், taken as கேவலத்தில் சுத்தம்.

2251.reading: Kevala within sakala is the state beyond waking; sakala within sakala is waking within waking; suddha within sakala is the state of the supreme; these three natures are within sakala.
2251.nuance: Here the three states meet the five of waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and beyond. சாக்கிரசாக்கிரம் (waking in waking) is ordinary bound life at its fullest.

2252.reading: Suddha within suddha is becoming the ancient Siva; kevala within suddha is the ancient stillness; sakala within suddha is the play of turiya; these three too can be told within suddha.
2252.nuance: உபசாந்தம் (stillness) and துரிய விலாசம் (turiya's play) are technical. The highest of the nine is becoming Siva, which I have marked as union.

2253.reading: Within waking-in-waking there is also dream; within waking there is deep sleep and turiya; in the state beyond waking there is easeful bliss; and the five impurity-bonds, concealment and the rest, make these.
2253.nuance: The waking states are nested inside waking, which is the jagrat-avastha scheme of Siddhanta as tradition gives it. மறையாதி (concealing and the rest) is taken as the concealing power, திரோதாயி, among the five.

2254.reading: In the state beyond waking, anava itself is cut off; that state does not remain in the para state; the stillness it brings, transcending, looks on the impurities and qualities and sees them.
2254.nuance: Lines 2 to 4 are obscure. பரோபதி may be 'beyond adjuncts'. The sense may be that the freed state witnesses the impurities without being bound by them.

2255.reading: Once one knows by grace that it is the Father's grace that, unseen, consumes bondage and release, the turiya that holds them and pure atita, there is no mind of one's own and no action of one's own.
2255.nuance: தோன்றாமல் தானுணும் (consumes them unseen) makes even the states of the soul the working of grace. அருளால் அறிந்தபின்: the knowing too is by grace. The end of mind and action is the sign, not the means.

2256.reading: Bondage and release, as they are called, both come by Hara's grace, as play and as the way that brings the soul to purity; so the soul comes to know in the Lord.
2256.nuance: The verse calls bondage itself grace (அருளே) and play (விளையாட்டு). In Siddhanta the impurities are bound to the soul so that they may ripen and fall; that is the tradition's account of why bondage could be called grace.

2257.reading: Those with five impurities are the sakalas reckoned; those with five impurities are bound by hard deeds; those with five impurities go on the path to heaven; those with five impurities are those who know Hara.
2257.nuance: The repeated ஐம்மலத்தார் places even heaven-goers under the impurities. The last line can mean that those still bound come to know Hara, or that they are known to him; neither reading is settled by the verse.

2258.reading: In the womb maya mixes in the beyond state; rare turiya and the desire that feeds in it, the sushumna and the first eight in the subtle body, and rare dream and the gross body are those.
2258.nuance: The verse maps the states onto the embryo and the body. கழுனை is read as சுழுனை (sushumna, or deep sleep), and எட்டும் சூக்கத்து as the eight of the subtle body; the last line is obscure.

2259.reading: Anava is in the beyond state; above it maya is borne in turiya; deep sleep has false karma; dream holds mahamaya; and the concealing power is seen in waking, where the impurities mix.
2259.nuance: Each of the five states is matched with one of five impurities. Where திரோதாயி belongs, with dream or with waking, depends on how line 3 is divided.

2260.reading: The knower beginning from Hara is in the beyond state; maya, from Hara on, stays in deep sleep; those who knew karma and took up mahamaya, and those who tell of grace, are in sakala.
2260.nuance: I can't make the syntax of this verse sure. It seems to place kinds of knowers and impurities across the states, as 2258 and 2259 do.

2261.reading: In sakala the soul takes a body, meets experience and what is experienced, settles among the elements, mind and the rest, holds to their working, dwells among sound and the other objects, and comes into the womb.
2261.nuance: போகம் and போக்கியம் are the enjoying and the enjoyed. The verse lists the sakala soul's equipment in order, ending at birth.

2262.reading: When the two deeds balance and sweet grace-power enters, establishing a seat in knowledge and taking the guru, grace-power joins one to itself, the great impurity goes, and purity is non-birth.
2262.nuance: இருவினை ஒப்பு (balance of the two deeds) and the descent of grace-power (சத்திநிபாதம்) are traditionally the conditions for the guru's coming. The verse nearly repeats 1527. Line 1 reads இருவிடை, taken as இருவினை.

2263.reading: When the soul reaches the end, the beyond-turiya, past the thirty-six, the six and the twenty-five with their states, the five who were his gain fade in the light, and ash-adorned supreme Siva comes to dwell in him.
2263.nuance: ஐவர் are traditionally the five deities presiding over the states, who withdraw. ஆதேயம் (what is held or placed in something) is taken as Siva becoming the content of the soul; the numbers in line 1 are uncertain.

2264.reading: Not knowing himself, he first took the body as himself; when he first saw himself, he saw turiya; but if the turiya he contemplates is not made one with the Lord, he will be born again.
2264.nuance: Three steps: body taken for self, self seen as turiya, turiya joined to the Lord. The verse warns that self-knowledge stopped at the second step still leads to birth.

2265.reading: If the beyond state is reached within waking, the bindu-born state it brings is bliss; looming birth is cut off, firm release is attained, and speech and mind do not reach it.
2265.nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் (beyond in waking) is traditionally taken as release while living in the body. வயிந்தவம் (bindu-born) here seems to name a pure state, not a bond.

2266.reading: Water and fire come within the breast; water and fire do not come within the breast; if you ask what water and fire are within the breast, they are water and fire mingled, that way.
2266.nuance: A riddle. அகலம் is breast or expanse, and அகல் a lamp, which holds oil and flame. Water and fire are taken symbolically as moon and sun, Shakti and Siva, or white bindu and red nada (compare 1929); none of these is stated.

2267.reading: Twenty-four are impure, seven pure-impure belong with maya, and five are pure; divided in these three parts, they are maya, mahamaya and what goes with the soul.
2267.nuance: The count 24 + 7 + 5 = 36 is the standard Siddhanta grouping of the tattvas. Which group line 4 assigns to the soul is not clear.

2268.reading: With maya as foster mother, mahamaya giving birth, and supreme Siva standing as father, the soul passes through kevala and sakala, and the purity it seeks comes to it of itself.
2268.nuance: கைத்தாய் is the nurse or foster mother. The family image gathers the chapter: the soul is raised through impure maya, born of pure maya and fathered by Siva, and the bound states are its upbringing. தான்வந்து அடையுமே: purity comes, it is not seized.

links.note: Both say a person is the maker of his own rise and fall: the Naladiyar names who sets a man up and casts him down and answers 'himself', Tirumular says he is his own enemy, friend, next world and master.
The Kural traces joyless birth to taking the unreal for the real; Tirumular's first error is the same kind, taking the body for the self, and it too ends in birth again.
2014 has the soul enter turiya and become knowledge; 2264 adds that turiya not joined to the Lord still leads back to birth.
Near-repetition: both open with the two deeds balancing and grace-power coming as or through the guru, and end with the impurities removed, as becoming Siva in 1527 and as non-birth here.
1924's numbers for the thirty-six tattvas do not add up as read; 2267 gives the standard grouping clearly, twenty-four impure, seven pure-impure and five pure.

2228 makes the soul answerable for itself: it eats the fruit of the deeds it did and is its own master (தானே தான்செய்த வினைப்பயன் துய்ப்பானும், தானே தனக்குத் தலைவனும்). 2628 says that in bondage and in release alike the soul has no task of its own (பெத்தத்தும் தன்பணி இல்லை ... முத்தத்தும் தன்பணி இல்லை), since the Father gives both by grace. The conflict holds if 2228's தலைவன் makes the soul master of its own bondage and release, not only answerable inside it.

The Kural says that one who loves himself should go near no evil deed, however small (தன்னைத்தான் காதலனாயின்). 2228 states the ground of that advice: the self is its own friend and enemy and itself eats the fruit of the deeds it did (தானே தனக்குப் பகைவனும் நட்டானும்).

Both verses list the sakalas, those joined to the three impurities, from Brahma and the gods through men down to the insect (மலரோன்மால் ... நரர் சீடம் / வேதா ... கீடாந்தத்து). 2244 adds that the sakalas enter the womb (யோனிபுக்கு), so the near-repeat ties the three impurities to birth.

Both verses place the hundred and eight Rudras (நூற்றெட்டு உருத்திரர்) among souls still in maya, 2231 with Srikantha in the pralaya class, 2243 in the sakala of anava, karma and mahamaya. The shared figure shows the chapter counting even high Rudras among bound souls, though the two verses do not settle which class they belong to.

2232 says those in kevala with anava alone are the vijnanakalas, Ananta and the other lords (கேவலத்து ஆணவத்து ஆனவர்). 498 opens its scheme the same way (விஞ்ஞானர் ஆணவ கேவல மேவுவோர்), from a chapter on the kinds of soul far earlier in the book.

1929 makes bindu, joined with Shakti and Siva, the power that grants release (வீடுஅளிக்கும் செயல்). 2233 says those graced by Siva leave bindu and nada behind as the impurity goes (விந்து நாதம் விட்டு) and so become stainless. The conflict holds on the reading that 2233 treats bindu as something release must leave, not as its giver.

115 says the soul and its bond cannot go to the Lord, but when the Lord draws near they do not remain (பதியணுகிற் பசு பாசம் நில்லாவே). 2234 ends on the same act: the Lord gathers the impurities and cuts them away (ஈசன் மலம் அறுத்தானே). In both the removal of the bond is the Lord's doing, not the soul's.

2235 calls the suddha state the soul's leaving the false thirty-six behind (பொய்யான போதாந்தம் ஆறாறும் விட்டகன்று) and reaching without reaching. 2308 says the good soul in turiya does not go into the evil thirty-six (பொல்லாத ஆறாறுள் போகாது) but reaches Siva's state. Both define purity as standing clear of the thirty-six tattvas.

2405 sets three things without beginning: the knowing soul, the Lord and the bond (அனாதி), and says birth ends when the soul rests in the Lord. 2236 repeats அனாதி for the soul, its five impurities, kevala and its births, yet ends in the suddha state. Together they show beginningless bondage is not endless.

2237 calls knowing oneself by oneself within turiya the reality itself (தன்பால் தனையறி தத்துவந் தானே). 2279 warns that birth does not end merely by knowing oneself (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாதால்), and points to the pervading Stainless one. The later verse puts a condition on the earlier: self-knowledge in turiya must go on to the Lord.

2238 says the twenty-five subside in the soul and the soul, seeing truth, finds release in the suddha state (ஐஐந்து ஒடுங்கும் ஆன்மாவில்). 2306 takes the step further: if the soul is Hara's son, the soul as a separate thing is gone and so are the twenty-five (ஆன்மாவும் இல்லையால் ஐஐந்தும் இல்லையே).

2197 counts the tattvas withdrawing in stages, the twenty-five and then the six, to make waking, dream and deep sleep (ஆறாறில் ஐஐந்து அகல ... ஆறாம் அவைவிட). 2239 uses the same count, the twenty-five with the six subsiding into the soul (ஐஐந்தும் ஆன்மாவில் ஆறோடு அடங்கி), but carries it past the states to Shakti in Siva's portion.

2192 names the three impurities, anava, maya and karma, and likens them to the bran and husk on the grain of the soul. 2240 sorts beings by how many of these they bear: anava alone for the kevalas, maya for the pralayakalas, all three for the sakalas (முப்பாசமும் புக்கோரே).

2245 has the bonds, the maddening darkness, let go by the ray that is Siva (மத்த இருள் சிவனான கதிராலே). 2293 has the five impurities leave like evening dark before a flame (சுடர்முனம் அந்தி இருள்போலும் ஐம்மலம்). Both picture purification as darkness giving way to light, the light in each being grace.

The Kural says stainless sight removes darkness and confusion and brings joy (இருள்நீங்கி ... மாசறு காட்சி). 2245 also has darkness end and purity come (மத்த இருள் ... சுத்தஆவார்கள்), but the light that ends it is Siva's ray, not the seer's own clear sight.

2247 describes kevala as the soul without knowledge, without action and pervaded by impurity (அறிவின்றி ... செயலிலான் ... மலவியாபி). 2162 calls the same state anava's sleep of utter stupor (அதிமூட நித்திரை ஆணவம்). Both make kevala a blank, not a freedom.

2249 says kevala, sakala and suddha each divide into three, making an unceasing nine (ஓவலில்லா ஒன்பான்). 498 likewise ends by counting the kinds of soul as nine (விஞ்ஞானராதிகள் ஒன்பான் வேறுயிர்களே). Both reach a ninefold scheme from the three states, 2249 by states within states, 498 by classes of soul.

2250 says that in the suddha within kevala, the Lord is there as the form of grace (ஆவயின் நாதன் அருண்மூர்த்தி). 2312 has the Father, with a grace that makes no division, stay joined to the soul left in kevala (வேறுசெய்யா அருள் கேவலத்தே விட்டு). Both find the Lord present by grace even in kevala.

2251 names kevala within sakala as the state beyond waking (சகலத்தில் கேவலம் சாக்கிராதீதம்). 2265 says what that state brings when reached: bliss, the end of birth and firm release beyond speech and mind (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம் தலைப்படில்).

2252 calls kevala within suddha the ancient stillness (சுத்தத்தில் கேவலம் தொல்லுபசாந்தமாம்). 2509, in the chapter named for that stillness, sets out what உபசாந்தம் contains: removing anava, knowing oneself, purity and the state beyond waking.

2254 says that in the state beyond waking anava itself is cut off (சாக்கிராதீதத்தில் தானறும் ஆணவம்). 2212 says that in that same state anava does not leave (சாக்கிராதீதத்தில் ஆணவம் தான்விடா). The conflict depends on reading both as the same state at the same stage; 2212 may mean the state before grace completes it.

2254 links the state beyond waking, where anava is cut off, with the stillness that looks on the impurities (உபசாந்தத்தை நோக்கும்). 2509 defines that stillness as removing anava and reaching the unspoken state beyond waking (கூறாத சாக்கிராதீதம் ... உபசாந்தமே).

2255 says that once one knows bondage and release are the Father's grace, there is no mind and no action of one's own (சித்தமும் இல்லை செயல்இல்லை). 2628 says the same from devotion: since the Father gives both bondage and release by grace, the devotee has no task (பணியொன்றும் இல்லையே).

2256 says bondage and release both come by Hara's grace (பெத்தமும் முத்தமும் ... அரன் அருளே). 2628 makes the same claim (அத்தற்கு இரண்டும் அருளால் அளித்தலால்) in the chapter on devotion, where it becomes the reason the devotee need do nothing.

2257 says those with five impurities go even on the path to heaven (ஐம்மலத்தார் சுவர்க்கந்நெறி யான்பவர்). 2337 says those still in the darkness of the five impurities go from earth to heaven and hell (பாரின்கண் விண்நரகம் புகும்), while those freed become Siva. Both count heaven as a place of the bound, not of release.

2258 says maya mixes the states into the soul in the womb, beginning with the beyond state and turiya (கருவில் அதீதம் கலப்பிக்கும் மாயை). 460 likewise has maya, in the womb, join her brood to the kevala soul and break turiya so thought arises (கர்ப்பத்துக் ... துரியமும் பேதித்து). Both place the soul's states in its embryonic beginning.

2259 matches the five impurities to five states: concealment in waking, mahamaya in dream, karma in deep sleep, maya in turiya, anava beyond. 2167 gives the same matches inside waking (திரோதாயி, மாமாயை, காமியம், மாயை), so the two verses apply one scheme at two scales.

2259 places maya in turiya and karma in deep sleep (பூணும் துரியம் ... சுழுத்திபொய்க் காமியம்). 2195 places karma in turiya (துரியம் சொல் காமியம்) and desire in deep sleep. Both agree that anava belongs beyond, but on the reading that each assigns one impurity per state, their turiya differs.

2144 lists what makes the bound waking state: the senses, their objects, the airs, the four inner instruments and the soul (பந்தஅச் சாக்கரம்). 2261 lists the sakala soul's equipment in nearly the same terms, body, elements, mind and the objects beginning with sound (சத்தாதி), and ends with entry into the womb.

The Kural defines purity as the absence of craving, which comes by wanting truth (தூஉய்மை என்பது அவாவின்மை). 2262 defines purity as non-birth (பிறவாமை சுத்தமே), reached when the two deeds balance, grace descends and the guru removes the great impurity. The verse puts purity's cause in grace, where the Kural puts it in the person's own ending of desire.

2263 has the soul pass the tattvas and states to the beyond-turiya, where supreme Siva comes to dwell in it (பரம்சிவம் ஆதேயமாகுமே). 2539 describes the end of the nine states the same way, with Siva-knowledge taking the place of the scattered impurities and the self becoming itself and not itself (நவமான அந்தத்தின் நற்சிவ போதம்).

A near-repeat: both open with the soul once taking the body as itself (உடலைமுன் தான்என்றான் / உடலைமுன் நான்ஒன்றாய்) and then seeing turiya. 2264 says turiya not made one with the Lord leads to rebirth; 2279 says birth does not end by self-knowledge alone. Both warn against stopping at the self.

2265 says that if the beyond is reached within waking, birth is cut off and release is firm (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம் தலைப்படில் ... நோன்முத்தி). 2302 places purity in the same faultless state beyond waking (தீதறு சாக்கிராதீதத்தில் சுத்தமே). Both set release inside the waking life, not after it.

Both verses play on water and fire (அப்பும் அனலும்) and their mixing (கலந்தது / கலப்பும்) as a riddle. 2581 adds that only the Knower present within makes one know it. The pairing suggests the riddle of 2266 is meant to be solved by inner teaching, not by reckoning.

2179 says the thirty-six are the Saivas' tattvas, against the counts of other schools (ஆறாறு அருஞ்சைவர் தத்துவம்). 2267 sets out how those thirty-six divide: twenty-four impure, seven pure-impure and five pure (அறுநான்கு அசுத்தம் ... ஐந்தே சுத்தம்).

Both use the figure of a child raised by a foster-mother (செவிலி / கைத்தாய்). In the Kural grace, born of love, is nursed by wealth; in 2268 the soul, born of mahamaya with Siva as father, is raised by maya. In both the nurse is a lower thing that serves a higher end.

source_issues: 2230: சீடம் is probably a misprint for கீடம் (worm, insect), as in 2244 (கீடாந்தத்து).
2250: line 3 reads கேவத் திறசுத்தம், apparently corrupt for கேவலத்தில் சுத்தம்.
2258: கழுனை is probably a misprint for சுழுனை (compare 2260).
2262: line 1 reads இருவிடை; the Sengalvaraya parallel and 1527 read இருவினை.
2237, 2246, 2248 and 2260 are obscure throughout and may be corrupt; 2239's நாலேழ் fits no count I can fix.
